scope: PEER side of the Ferric parity audit for engine (E*), format (F*), backend (B*), model-class (M*) features
method: Depth-1 clones of each peer's GitHub repo (commits pinned in peers{}), README + docs/ + source read this session; official doc sites fetched where cited. Evidence URLs point at the pinned commit.

llama.cpp.summary: C/C++ LLM/VLM inference engine on ggml: CLI, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible llama-server, GGUF conversion + quantization tools, 17 backends incl. CUDA/HIP/Metal/Vulkan/SYCL/WebGPU/Hexagon/CANN.

vLLM.summary: Python/PyTorch LLM serving engine (PagedAttention, continuous batching) for datacenter GPUs, with CPU backends and out-of-tree hardware/format plugins.

SGLang.summary: Python/PyTorch LLM and multimodal serving framework (RadixAttention prefix cache, zero-overhead scheduler, PD disaggregation, large-scale EP) for NVIDIA/AMD GPUs, Xeon CPUs, Ascend NPUs, TPU (via SGLang-JAX) and Apple Silicon (MLX).

TensorRT-LLM.summary: NVIDIA's open-source LLM (and visual-generation) inference library for NVIDIA GPUs only (Ampere-Blackwell); PyTorch is now the sole backend (the TensorRT engine backend was removed), aimed at datacenter serving (trtllm-serve, Dynamo, Triton).

MLX / mlx-lm.summary: Apple's MLX array framework (Metal, CUDA and CPU backends; mx.distributed over ring/JACCL/MPI/NCCL) plus mlx-lm, its Python package for LLM generation, quantization, fine-tuning and an OpenAI-style HTTP server.

mistral.rs.summary: Pure-Rust (candle-based) LLM/multimodal inference engine with CLI, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible server, Python and Rust SDKs; CUDA, Metal and CPU backends.

candle.summary: Hugging Face's minimalist Rust ML framework (tensors + model zoo as examples), inference-focused, CUDA/Metal/CPU/WASM; no serving engine in-repo (README defers to external candle-vllm, vllm.rs).

ExLlamaV3.summary: Python/PyTorch + CUDA/Triton inference library for consumer NVIDIA GPUs built around the EXL3 (QTIP-derived trellis) quantization format; dynamic batching generator, TP/EP, CPU MoE offload; TabbyAPI is the recommended OpenAI-compatible server on top.

KTransformers.summary: Tsinghua MADSys/Approaching.AI CPU-GPU heterogeneous MoE inference and fine-tuning. Current inference = kt-kernel CPU expert kernels (AMX/AVX512/AVX2/llamafile/BLIS) inside a SGLang fork (sglang-kt); the original integrated framework is archived.

LMDeploy.summary: InternLM/OpenMMLab toolkit for compressing and serving LLMs/VLMs with two engines: TurboMind (C++/CUDA, NVIDIA only) and PyTorchEngine (Python; CUDA, ROCm, Ascend, Cambricon, MetaX).

MLC-LLM / WebLLM.summary: TVM-based ML compiler + MLCEngine (OpenAI-compatible, Python/REST/iOS/Android) that compiles models ahead of time per GPU target (CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan, Metal, OpenCL, WebGPU); WebLLM is its in-browser WebGPU TypeScript engine.

ExecuTorch.summary: PyTorch's on-device inference stack: torch.export -> backend-delegated .pte run by a small C++ runtime across CPU (XNNPACK), GPU (Vulkan, Metal/MLX, CUDA, WebGPU) and NPUs/DSPs (Core ML, QNN, MediaTek, Samsung, Arm, NXP, Cadence, OpenVINO), with LLM runners and experimental batching/serving.

LiteRT-LM.summary: Google's on-device LLM orchestration layer over LiteRT: runs pre-converted .litertlm models on CPU (XNNPACK), GPU (OpenCL/WebGPU/Metal) and NPU (Qualcomm, MediaTek, Google Tensor, Samsung, Intel) with C++/Kotlin/Swift/Python/JS APIs, plus an omni ASR/TTS engine.

MNN.summary: Alibaba's on-device deep-learning inference/training framework, with MNN-LLM (llmexport converter + C++ runtime) for single-sequence LLM/VLM/omni/TTS/ASR/embedding inference on phones/PC/web. It targets CPU (ARM/x86), Metal/OpenCL/Vulkan/CUDA and NPUs (QNN, Hexagon, MTK NeuroPilot, CoreML, HiAI, NNAPI, RKNN), and ships MNN Chat apps for Android and iOS. Models must be exported to .mnn first.

Colibri.summary: Pure-C inference ENGINE plus research platform (Python launcher/OpenAI+Anthropic gateway, web dashboard, Tauri desktop shell) for frontier MoE models (GLM-5.2/5.3, Inkling, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Qwen3.6/3.8, OLMoE). One C engine per model family. Routed experts are staged across VRAM, RAM and NVMe (streamed from SSD, learned pinning, prefetch), with optional CUDA/HIP, Metal and Vulkan tiers. Not a router or wrapper.

FreeToken.summary: Python + CUDA/Triton MoE serving ENGINE (derived from mini-sglang, reuses SGLang/vLLM/FlashInfer code) for running large open MoE models on one consumer NVIDIA GPU (experimental AMD). Experts are offloaded to host RAM with a GPU LRU cache and bandwidth-adaptive CPU/GPU hybrid execution. Continuous batching with radix/paged KV and CUDA graphs; OpenAI/Anthropic/Responses APIs; `ft` CLI plus a Windows/Linux desktop app. Not a router or wrapper.

exo.summary: Python/Rust cluster orchestrator that auto-discovers devices and shards one model across them (tensor or pipeline parallel over MLX distributed ring/JACCL RDMA-over-Thunderbolt); engine is MLX via a fork of mlx-lm (rltakashige/mlx-lm@leo/deepseek-v4) plus mlx-vlm, and mflux for images. No tinygrad engine located at this commit.

burn / CubeCL.summary: Rust deep-learning framework (training + inference, autodiff, automatic kernel fusion) on the CubeCL JIT kernel language/runtime (CUDA, ROCm, Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU, CPU); general building blocks, no LLM engine in-repo (Burn-LM archived; pretrained models in separate tracel-ai/models).

peer_notes.candle: No serving engine or continuous batching located in README/candle-book/source; README points to external candle-vllm / vllm.rs / atoma-infer for serving.
peer_notes.ExLlamaV3: 'Continuous, dynamic batching'; Generator(max_batch_size=256) schedules concurrent jobs over a shared paged cache.
peer_notes.KTransformers: Delegated to the sglang-kt fork (third_party/sglang submodule, not present in the clone): KT docs launch with --max-running-requests and --enable-mixed-chunk; README perf row at 8-way concurrency. The archived framework had its own C++ continuous-batching scheduler (doc/en/balance-serve.md#L20).
peer_notes.LMDeploy: TurboMind 'persistent batch' (= continuous batching); PyTorchEngine continuous batching (inference/pytorch.md#L54).
peer_notes.MLC-LLM / WebLLM: BatchDecode action runs one decode step for every request in the engine running_queue; new-request prefill is interleaved (prefill_mode 'hybrid' = split-fuse, default). Mode 'server' auto-sizes max batch (python/mlc_llm/serve/config.py#L25-L45).
peer_notes.ExecuTorch: Experimental (ET_EXPERIMENTAL) batching Runner: DecodeFirstScheduler batches decodes of up to max_decode_sequences sessions, then fills the token budget with prefill chunks. ModuleExecutor is implemented for the MLX off-graph cache only (extension/llm/batching/README.md#L141); examples/llm_server CUDA workers host several sessions but execute serially.
peer_notes.LiteRT-LM: Multiple sessions share one LlmExecutor via context-handler switching (AcquireExecutorWithContextHandler); num_output_candidates is a decode batch of candidates for one prompt. No iteration-level batching of different requests located.
peer_notes.MNN: Not located. MNN-LLM drives one sequence per Llm instance; the bundled HTTP server (mls_server) serializes requests behind llm_mutex_. Several independent Llm instances can run in threads (engine/test/test_multi_instance.cpp) but there is no iteration-level batching of different requests.
peer_notes.Colibri: Only the GLM-5.2 engine (c/colibri.c run_serve_mux, used by the HTTP gateway via SERVE_BATCH=1) batches decode continuously across up to 16 KV slots, one row per active slot per forward. Prefill stays serial (colibri.c#L9168). The other family engines have no mux path, and docs/api.md#L78 still says the server serves one generation at a time. Colibri's own experiment found aggregate throughput saturates at the single-stream ceiling.
peer_notes.FreeToken: The scheduler batches every running request into each decode step (mini-sglang lineage). --max-running-requests defaults to 4 (docs/cli.md#L44).
peer_notes.exo: ExoBatchGenerator wraps mlx-lm's continuous-batching BatchGenerator (runner/llm_inference/batch_generator.py BatchGenerator engine). TODO.md item 7: a new prompt's prefill still blocks decode of the running batch.
peer_notes.burn / CubeCL: No serving engine or batching scheduler in burn/cubecl. Burn-LM (the prior LLM engine, separate repo tracel-ai/burn-lm) is archived per its README (gh api, a53baab).

peer_notes.llama.cpp: Automatic, on by default: cache_prompt reuses the common prefix of a slot's KV (README L587, --cache-prompt L220); --slot-prompt-similarity routes to the best-matching slot; host-RAM prompt cache (--cache-ram, default 8192 MiB, L167) restores the cached prompt with the longest common prefix. Mechanism is longest-common-prefix scan + state copy/restore, not radix tree/hash blocks; --cache-reuse adds chunk reuse via KV shifting (L221).
peer_notes.vLLM: Automatic Prefix Caching; hash-based per KV block (parent hash + block tokens + extra hashes), docs/design/prefix_caching.md L5-19. Enabled via enable_prefix_caching.
peer_notes.SGLang: RadixAttention (radix-tree prefix cache); --disable-radix-cache (server_arguments.mdx L2398); session-aware radix cache and cache-aware router.
peer_notes.TensorRT-LLM: Filled blocks stored in a radix search tree and reused across requests; enabled by default (enable_block_reuse), partial-block reuse, priority-LRU eviction, cache_salt isolation.
peer_notes.MLX / mlx-lm: Server keeps an LRUPromptCache backed by a token PromptTrie; fetch_nearest_cache reuses the longest cached prefix (trimming longer trimmable caches) across requests. Also explicit mlx_lm.cache_prompt files.
peer_notes.mistral.rs: Paged mode: reference-counted shared prefix blocks; non-paged: whole-sequence prefix cache (--prefix-cache-n, default 16). README: prefix caching including multimodal.
peer_notes.candle: No prefix caching located.
peer_notes.ExLlamaV3: Pages keyed by chained blake2b content hashes are deduplicated and reused across jobs (prompt-cache hits).
peer_notes.KTransformers: Archived framework: 3-layer GPU-CPU-Disk prefix cache (README#L47). Current KT docs only mention turning SGLang's radix cache off (--disable-radix-cache, DeepSeek-V4-Flash.md#L179), and the Ascend guide says prefix caching is unsupported with a split expert set.
peer_notes.LMDeploy: enable_prefix_caching (block-level reuse) in both engines (PytorchEngineConfig.enable_prefix_caching); off by default.
peer_notes.MLC-LLM / WebLLM: prefix_cache_mode 'radix' (paged radix-tree prefix cache) is the default; cpp/serve/radix_tree.cc + prefix_cache.cc.
peer_notes.ExecuTorch: batching::PrefixCache: bounded LRU of snapshot sessions matched by longest token prefix, cloned into new sessions. Caller-owned, opt-in (--prefix_cache_entries), implemented for MLX; llm_server CUDA workers do not use it.
peer_notes.LiteRT-LM: CachedSession: automatic longest-common-prefix reuse (text tokens plus image/audio hashes) against that session's own history, with rewind; not a shared cross-request radix/hash pool.
peer_notes.MNN: Single-session only. reuse_kv (documented) keeps the KV across turns. prompt_cache (source, llm.cpp#L1219) prefills only the suffix after the longest common prefix with the previous turn. rollback_demo caches a shared-prefix KV to disk (llm.md#L839). No radix/hash cache across concurrent requests.
peer_notes.Colibri: Automatic per-slot longest-common-prefix KV reuse across HTTP requests, even across restarts. Opt-in cross-slot prefix copy COLI_KV_SHARE (colibri.c#L9322, described as 'RadixAttention's benefit at memcpy cost'). DSV4 prefix checkpoints in memory and on disk. No shared radix/hash block cache.
peer_notes.FreeToken: --cache-type radix (default) prefix reuse, with SWA- and GDN-aware radix variants. --enable-cache-report reports hits.
peer_notes.exo: KVPrefixCache: longest-prefix match across requests with LRU eviction under memory pressure, media-region validation for vision prompts; disabled by default on the /bench endpoint.
peer_notes.burn / CubeCL: Not located.

peer_notes.vLLM: 'In V1, chunked prefill is enabled by default whenever possible'; decode-first scheduling with max_num_batched_tokens budget.
peer_notes.SGLang: --chunked-prefill-size (-1 disables); dynamic chunking with PP.
peer_notes.TensorRT-LLM: Chunked context via LLM(enable_chunked_prefill=True).
peer_notes.MLX / mlx-lm: Prompts are processed in --prefill-step-size chunks (default 2048); BatchGenerator._next interleaves one decode step with one prefill chunk for waiting prompts.
peer_notes.mistral.rs: CUDA text prompts are chunked from a batch-wide token budget (--max-prefill-chunk-tokens, default 512). Docs: limit does not change CPU or Metal scheduling, so CUDA-only.
peer_notes.candle: No chunked prefill in the serving sense. mamba2's '--use-prefill ... chunked prefill' is the SSD chunked scan over the whole prompt in one forward; quantized examples offer --split-prompt (token-by-token).
peer_notes.ExLlamaV3: max_chunk_size (default 2048) caps prefill tokens per pass so a new job only briefly interrupts ongoing jobs.
peer_notes.KTransformers: --chunked-prefill-size in all current launch examples (delegated to sglang-kt); KTMoEWrapper(chunked_prefill_size=...) in kt-kernel; archived balance_serve chunked prefill.
peer_notes.LMDeploy: TurboMind 'Dynamic SplitFuse'-like scheduling (num_tokens_per_iter, max_prefill_iters, max_prefill_token_num); PyTorchEngine long-context chunked prefill (lmdeploy/pytorch/paging/prefill_scheduler.py).
peer_notes.MLC-LLM / WebLLM: prefill_mode 'chunked' or 'hybrid' (split-fuse); prefill_chunk_size (L88).
peer_notes.ExecuTorch: Prefill split into max_prefill_chunk_size chunks rotated across sessions; MLX export --prefill-chunk-size (backends/mlx/examples/llm/README.md#L100).
peer_notes.LiteRT-LM: CpuConfig.prefill_chunk_size for dynamically exported models; GPU/NPU use fixed prefill signatures.
peer_notes.MNN: The `chunk` / `chunk_limits` config splits prompt processing into chunks to cap memory (llm.cpp#L146). The engine serves one sequence, so chunks are not interleaved with other requests' decode.
peer_notes.Colibri: COLI_PREFILL_CHUNK slices a long prompt into N-token chunks with byte-identical output. K3_CHUNK and GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK in sibling engines. These are memory slices, not interleaved with other requests' decode.
peer_notes.FreeToken: --max-prefill-length sets the chunked-prefill chunk size (default 8192).
peer_notes.exo: Prefill runs in prefill_step_size chunks (4096 in batch path); pipeline_parallel_prefill overlaps chunks across pipeline ranks. Not interleaved with running decodes (TODO.md item 7).

notes: METHOD: 18 peers x 73 features (E01-E29, F01-F17, B01-B16, M01-M11) = 1314 cells. Depth-1 clones of 21 repos taken 2026-09-27 (commits in peers{}); README, docs/ and source read this session by six peer-group passes, then merged, cross-checked and reconciled here. 874 of 878 GitHub evidence URLs were machine-checked to resolve to an existing file and line in the pinned clones; the other 4 point at sibling repos (vllm-gguf-plugin, tracel-ai/models) and were checked with gh api. 40+ cited lines were read back by hand. Non-GitHub URLs (vllm.ai/blog, lmsys.org, blog.mlc.ai) were WebFetched by the passes that cite them. STATUS: have = the peer's own README/docs/source shows it; partial = part of it (peer_notes says which); lack = not located in README/docs/source at the pinned commit (an absence finding of this review, not a claim that it cannot exist); unclear = evidence conflicts or depends on unaudited code. 'via_plugin_or_sibling' marks have/partial cells that exist only through an official plugin, sibling repo or wrapped engine the peer's docs name (vLLM hardware/format plugins, KTransformers -> sglang-kt fork, exo -> mlx-lm fork, SGLang -> KTransformers kernels, TRT-LLM -> ModelOpt). RULINGS applied to every peer: E02 needs a page/block table (llama.cpp-style cell pools = lack); E07 have needs a generic small-LM draft model (trained DFlash/assistant drafters only = partial; DFlash tallied separately as XE01); E12 have needs real pipelining (a plain sequential layer split = partial); E16 generic mmap paging = partial; E17 have needs layers computed on CPU (weights streamed to GPU for GPU compute = partial); E25 per-request adapter choice without mixed-adapter batches = partial; E27 a seed alone is not determinism; F-formats dequantized at load/convert with no runtime kernel = partial; F16/F17 done only by a sibling tool the docs point to = partial; M11 Whisper-only = partial. Six cells were changed by these rulings after the passes (see reconciliations). PUBLISHED NUMBERS: 73 figures, all copied from the peer's own README/docs/blog with URL and stated conditions; none computed here. They are not comparable with each other (different models, GPUs, baselines). Several are not feature on/off comparisons: SGLang GB200 3.8x/4.8x compares hardware; LMDeploy 'up to 1.8x vs vLLM' credits several features jointly; LiteRT-LM's MTP 'up to 3x' comes from a Google blog measured across several runtimes; exo's TP figures state no conditions; ExecuTorch TQ4 and SGLang FP4-KV figures are memory capacity, not speed. ADDED: 14 features several peers share that are not on features.tsv (XE01-XE13, XM01); only peers with a located citation are listed, others were not assessed. Proposals that duplicate existing ids are mapped in added_mapped_to_existing_ids. CAVEATS: KTransformers' current engine is a git-submodule SGLang fork absent from the clone, so its cells credit only what KT's own docs show; ExLlamaV3's serving features (API) live in TabbyAPI (not audited); mlx-vlm, mlx-examples, mlx-swift, vLLM-Omni, sglang-omni and candle-vllm are separate repos and were not credited except where noted.
part_notes: part1.json: No E* performance figures are published in the README/docs of llama.cpp, candle, burn or CubeCL at these commits (llama.cpp docs/speculative.md shows sample acceptance-rate logs only and points to the SPEED-Bench client; candle/burn docs give no E* numbers; CubeCL book speedups are tutorial reduction kernels, not E* features), so published_numbers is empty. candle and burn are ML frameworks, not serving engines: most E* serving features are 'lack' by design; candle's README points to external candle-vllm/vllm.rs/atoma-infer, and burn's LLM engine Burn-LM (tracel-ai/burn-lm, a53baab) is archived. For burn, M06/M08/M04/M10 consulted the separate tracel-ai/models README via gh api (commit 86f1628); only first-party 'official' models were credited (MiniLM, RoBERTa, ALBERT), community links (llama2-burn, whisper-burn, rwkv-burn) were not. llama.cpp converter (conversion/base.py) ingests FP8, GPTQ, compressed-tensors, BitNet, MXFP4 and NVFP4 HF checkpoints, but FP8/GPTQ/compressed-tensors are dequantized at conversion time (partial), while MXFP4/NVFP4/ternary have native GGML types (have). Judgment calls: llama.cpp E02 'lack' (cell-based unified KV, no page tables); E03 'have' although the mechanism is LCP scan + state restore rather than radix/hash; E25 'partial' because the docs say different-LoRA requests are not batched together; candle E02 'partial' for the paged flash-attn kernel without a KV block manager; candle/burn E24 and E26 per the notes.

part2.json: Sources: shallow clones at the listed commits (README, docs/, source), plus gh api reads of vllm-project/vllm-gguf-plugin (README at e2b8ad53) and repo descriptions of vllm-bnb-plugin, bart-plugin, vllm-metal; WebFetch of vllm.ai/blog posts (blog.vllm.ai now 301-redirects to vllm.ai/blog) and lmsys.org/blog posts cited in published_numbers. Markdown evidence URLs use ?plain=1#Lnn so line anchors resolve on GitHub. Delegation convention: a capability delivered by an official out-of-tree plugin or sibling repo that the peer's own docs document is marked 'have' with the delegation named in the note (vLLM: GGUF, bitsandbytes, Metal/MLX, TPU, Ascend/Rebellions/Spyre/Gaudi, BART; SGLang: TPU via SGLang-JAX, CPU experts via kt_kernel). Where only a sibling tool (vLLM llm-compressor, sglang-omni) provides it and the peer's runtime does not, the status is 'partial' or 'lack' with the reason. Weight offload (E15-E17): both engines keep compute on the GPU and stream weights from pinned host RAM, which is not llama.cpp's n-gpu-layers / --cpu-moe model where offloaded work runs on the CPU; hence 'partial'. SGLang is the exception for E15 via its KTransformers wrapper (CPU experts run on AMX/AVX). vLLM GGUF moved out of core into vllm-gguf-plugin (in-tree support deprecated, vllm issue 39583); vLLM bitsandbytes likewise moved to vllm-bnb-plugin. Published figures are recorded as the peers state them and were not reproduced.

part3.json: Scope and judgment calls. (1) TensorRT-LLM at e0448239 is PyTorch-only: the TensorRT engine backend, trtllm-build and convert_checkpoint.py were removed (docs/source/legacy/tensorrt-backend-removal.md), so legacy-engine features (weight streaming, ONNX/engine paths, INT8 SmoothQuant engines) were not credited. Its own quantization is delegated to NVIDIA Model Optimizer, a separate repo, so F16 is partial and F17 lack. GPTQ/AWQ count as partial because only ModelOpt-exported checkpoints map; there is no HF quant_method 'gptq'/'awq' branch. (2) LMDeploy has two engines and many features are engine-specific, noted per cell. PyTorchEngine only: speculative decoding (E07-E09), PD disaggregation (E23), LoRA (E25), the external KV connector (E28), TurboQuant/FP8 KV, ROCm, Ascend/Cambricon/MACA and SDAR dLLM. TurboMind only: GPTQ/compressed-tensors/MXFP4 loading and dynamic-NTK RoPE. The docs say TurboMind lacks window attention, but its kernel has a window_size param. (3) KTransformers is a wrapper. Current inference is kt-kernel (CPU MoE kernels) plugged into the kvcache-ai SGLang fork (sglang-kt, third_party/sglang submodule, NOT present in the clone). Per the wrapper rule, SGLang features count as 'have' only where KT's own docs expose the flag, with the delegation noted; SGLang features KT does not expose are 'lack'. The original integrated framework (balance_serve, 3-layer GPU-CPU-Disk prefix cache, long-context sparse attention, ROCm/Intel Arc XPU, injection multi-GPU) is archived under archive/ 'for reference' and its docs are commented out of doc/SUMMARY.md, so features found only there are marked 'partial' with 'archived' in the note. (4) E18: all three mmap safetensors/GGUF at load time; only KTransformers' CPU MoE computes directly from the mmap. The other two copy weights to GPU. (5) E24: TRT-LLM and LMDeploy document state snapshots/checkpoints for prefix reuse; KTransformers only runs the hybrid models. (6) Published numbers are copied from the peers' README/docs/blogs; several LMDeploy README figures give no hardware.

part4.json: Peer-side only; all statuses read from the pinned shallow clones listed in INSTRUCTIONS.md (no web fetches). Judgment calls applied consistently across these four peers: (1) 'layer split across GPUs' with no micro-batch pipelining = E12 partial (mistral.rs, ExLlamaV3); mlx-lm and exo have an explicit pipeline mode = have. (2) Seeded sampling alone is not E27; ExLlamaV3 gets partial for documented run-to-run bit-reproducibility (not batch invariance). (3) Dequantize-at-load of FP8/MXFP4 source checkpoints without a runtime kernel = partial (mlx-lm FP8, ExLlamaV3 FP8/MXFP4). (4) exo wrapper rule: exo runs MLX via a FORK of mlx-lm (rltakashige/mlx-lm@leo/deepseek-v4, pyproject.toml L96) plus mlx-vlm and mflux; features are credited only where exo source/docs/model cards reference them; always-on kernel features it inherits (fused SDPA, mx.compile) are marked partial 'implicit'; checkpoint formats exo never mentions (FP8, GPTQ, AWQ, compressed-tensors) are 'unclear' because they depend on the unaudited fork. No tinygrad engine exists in exo at this commit (0 hits). (5) 'MLX / mlx-lm' was audited as one peer: mlx-lm is text-only for VLM checkpoints (sanitize() drops the vision tower); vision lives in the separate mlx-vlm package, and Whisper in mlx-examples, neither audited. Surprises: mistral.rs REMOVED generic target/draft speculative decoding ('Legacy target/draft speculative decoding has been removed'); only MTP heads and MTP/DFlash assistant checkpoints remain. mistral.rs docs explicitly say GGUF IQ types are unsupported. exo has an undocumented, feature-flagged disaggregated prefill/decode path (ENABLE_DISAGGREGATION=true) with KV + SSM-snapshot transfer over TCP; its README says Linux runs CPU-only while pyproject ships mlx-cuda extras and a MlxCuda backend. exo samples system power per bench run (src/exo/utils/power_sampler.py) - the only energy telemetry among these four. ExLlamaV3 is the only one of the four with a second-tier CPU KV page cache (E28), expert parallelism (E14) and CPU MoE offload (E15); its CPU kernels are AVX-only (stubbed on aarch64). mlx-lm's quantized KV cache and draft-model speculation both disable server batching (served one request at a time). mistral.rs embedding Pooling: CLS/max/weighted-mean branches are unimplemented!(); only mean(sum)+last-token work.

part5.json: Clones read at the pinned commits with /usr/bin/grep. MLC-LLM and WebLLM are scored as one peer; a feature counts if either repo has it (WebLLM-only evidence is labelled). Engines built by compilation (MLC, ExecuTorch, LiteRT-LM) all need a conversion or export step, so F03 is 'lack' for all three, with notes. For F04-F06 'checkpoints' means loading pre-quantized third-party checkpoints; each peer's own quantizers are noted separately. For F07/F08/F11/F13 a format the peer produces with its own quantizer counts as have or partial, as noted. ExecuTorch's LLM serving features (batching, prefix cache, cell cache) are marked ET_EXPERIMENTAL and implemented only for the MLX executor. MLC's multi-node pipeline-parallel support (E13) is in source only and not in docs/. LiteRT-LM's GPU/NPU kernels ship as closed prebuilt libraries, so attention-kernel questions (E06) are unclear. LiteRT-LM M02 relies on the linked Google blog to identify Gemma 4 26B A4B as MoE. Published numbers come from blogs the peers link or run (blog.mlc.ai, blog.google).

part6.json: Assigned peers: MNN, Colibri, FreeToken; all 73 features filled for each. Commits verified against the clone HEADs. What each project is: (1) Colibri (JustVugg/colibri) is an inference engine (pure C, one engine per MoE family) plus research harness. It is not a router or wrapper. Its gateway is Python and CPU is the default backend. Several capabilities exist in only one of its nine engines, marked partial or noted: continuous batching (GLM only; docs/api.md#L78 contradicts serve_protocol.md), YaRN/SWA/sinks (DeepSeek V4 only), MTP (GLM/DSV4). Colibri's TP4 and TP2xPP3 numbers in docs/experiments are vLLM-Moet baselines, not Colibri features, so they are not recorded. (2) FreeToken (FlashML-org/FreeToken) is an engine (Python + CUDA/Triton, mini-sglang lineage) for one NVIDIA GPU. It is not a router. Its README/docs publish no E-feature figures; the linked paper abstract (arXiv 2608.16157, loaded) gives capability claims only (35B on laptop GPUs, 284B on gaming desktops, 753B GLM-5.2 on one workstation GPU, 20+ MoE models), so nothing was recorded. Tensor parallel exists in source but is undocumented and refused for quantized MoE formats, so it is partial. GGUF is Gemma-4-only and source-only. (3) MNN: every capability is scored for MNN-LLM where the LLM docs cover it. Backends B10 (CoreML) and B12 use the general MNN backend docs. MNN needs an export step (torch to ONNX to .mnn, or gguf2mnn/safetensors2mnn), hence F03 lack and F01 partial. MNN's --awq/--hqq are its own quantizers: counted under F17 (AWQ/Smooth/Omni) and F11 partial (HQQ), not as loading AWQ/HQQ checkpoints (F06 lack). Hints verified: 'MNN Chat on Android/iOS' is true. 'CoreML/ANE?' is partial (general backend, no LLM doc). 'QNN/NPU' is true, plus a new Hexagon backend (3.6.1) and MTK NeuroPilot. 'HIAI' is true (general). 'Qwen-Omni, speech/TTS, diffusion' are true (diffusion means image/video, not diffusion LLMs). Both 'MNN supports only CPU/METAL/OPENCL' (llm_bench doc) and CUDA/Vulkan LLM mentions (export C4 note) appear in docs; B01/B04 marked have with that caveat. Evidence URLs are pinned to the listed commits.

reconciliations.why: RULE E07: a generic small-LM draft model = have; only specially trained drafters (DFlash, assistant/MTP) = partial (same ruling as mistral.rs, LMDeploy, MNN). ExecuTorch's separate draft checkpoint is the DFlash block-diffusion drafter only; no generic draft-model path located (searched README, extension/llm, examples).

RULE E02: a llama.cpp-style shared pool of per-token cells without a page/block table is not a paged KV cache (same ruling as llama.cpp E02). CellCache (extension/llm/cache/README.md#L132) shares one cell pool across sequences.

RULE E25: several adapters selectable per request but never batched together = partial (same ruling as llama.cpp). mlx_lm.server takes a per-request 'adapters' path; a batch only holds requests with the same (model, adapter, draft) key.

RULE F16/F17: calibration done by a sibling project the peer's own docs direct users to = partial, via sibling (same ruling as vLLM + llm-compressor). TRT-LLM docs: 'To quantize your own model, use the NVIDIA TensorRT Model Optimizer Hugging Face export flow'.

RULE E16: generic mmap paging of weights from disk (not expert-aware) = partial (same ruling as llama.cpp E16). MNN use_mmap maps weights to disk under memory pressure; no expert-specific streaming located.

--split-mode layer (default) is documented as 'Pipeline parallelism' (docs/multi-gpu.md#L25), and the scheduler enables real pipelining with async compute across devices when all layers are offloaded (src/llama-context.cpp#L428-L456). This is why llama.cpp is have while mistral.rs / ExLlamaV3 plain sequential layer splits are partial.
